Subject: Re: Meridian DPA redlines and SCC comments — initial legal notes

Karthik / team — thanks, reviewed the redline and attached questions. Quick summary of legal's position and recommended carve-ins: 

1) SCCs: We can accept the 2021 SCCs but we need to preserve Redwood's standard Processor Annex and the subprocessor flow-down; propose we adopt Meridian's SCCs with Redwood Annex A/B mapping instead of their proposed role swaps.

2) Roles & purposes: Meridian redlined controller/processor roles in a way that would make Redwood a joint controller for usage analytics. That would increase liability and changes obligations (data subject requests, deletion). Recommend we keep Redwood as Processor for customer data and accept limited Controller status for aggregated, de-identified analytics where applicable — propose alternate language in §2.2 of the DPA.

3) Breach notifications: 3 business days is aggressive given forensic timelines. Recommend 72 hours for initial notification (within 72 hours of discovery) and follow-ups as facts develop; maintain the 3-business-day operational SLA only for high-severity incidents (we can agree to immediate operational notice via phone).

4) Audit & access: Meridian wants broad audit rights and continuous onsite audits. We should offer annual audit rights and questionnaire-based remote audits; provide SOC 2 Type II report as primary evidence and permit on-site reviews only with reasonable advance notice and scope limitation.

5) Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA): We can fill their questionnaire and run an internal TIA. If transfers are to EEA/UK, we can rely on SCCs + technical and organisational measures (encryption at rest/in transit, key management, data localisation options on Dedicated solutions).

Next steps I recommend: (a) Monica to complete Meridian's TIA questions and provide draft TIA findings; (b) Legal to prepare a redline counterdocument that: accepts SCC baseline, modifies breach timing and audit scope, preserves Redwood Annex structure. We should propose a short call with Meridian legal to walk the changes.

I can draft the counter by tomorrow afternoon if Monica provides the security notes.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Team,

I've completed Meridian_TIA_Questions_20260822.pdf and attached a short risk memo. Summary:

- Transfers: Redwood stores customer content primarily in us-west-2 for Meridian. For European subject data we can pin region on Dedicated; for Hosted customers we provide contractual SCCs + encryption.
- Encryption: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256); customer-managed keys available for Dedicated/Private.
- Subprocessors: Primary subprocessors are cloud providers and a managed logging vendor — list in memo. We are willing to publish a running subprocessor list and provide 30-days notice of changes.
- Deletion: We support deletion requests and have documented retention schedules; for e-discovery requests we'll engage legal.

Open items for Meridian to confirm: whether they require on-premises processing for specific data classes (PHI/PII) and whether the three-business-day SLA is non-negotiable.

I will attach the filled questionnaire to the counter DPA.

Carlos / Julia — thanks for the redlines and patience while we reviewed. Short summary and proposed path to signature: 

1) SCCs: Redwood can accept Meridian's use of the 2021 SCCs as the baseline. We'll provide a counter that preserves Redwood's Annex mapping (processor/subprocessor flow-down).

2) Roles & purpose: We cannot accept joint-controller treatment for standard usage analytics. We will propose language that keeps Redwood as Processor for customer data, and allows limited controller status only where data is irreversibly aggregated/anonymous.

3) Breach timing: We propose an initial notification within 72 hours of detection (and immediate operational updates for critical incidents via phone). We will offer to include a 3-business-day requirement for prioritized high-severity incident acknowledgement if that helps procurement.

4) Audit: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II report and accept annual remote assessments. On-site audits available with reasonable notice and scope bounds.

5) TIA: Monica attached our completed questionnaire and risk memo. We can run an internal TIA and share final findings; we can also accommodate data localisation on Dedicated/Private if Meridian requires it for regulated data.

Next steps: Laura & I will send Redwood's counter DPA by EOD today showing these changes. If Meridian can review and confirm acceptance of the SCC baseline + the adjusted breach/audit language we can finalize commercials and push to DocuSign (link included below).
